_note: SIEVE POINT, criterion A6. One independent study per grid point: ground rule
2 holds ACROSS cells, so no sample, stream or constant is shared between
them. The grid is uniform on [0, 1/2] and was fixed before reading anyone
else's phase diagram.
[0, 1/2] is the whole sieve: |X_k| has the SAME LAW at p and 1 - p
(particle-hole symmetry composed with reflection -- see
tools/tests/test_rwre.py::test_abs_displacement_has_the_same_law_at_p_and_one_minus_p),
so the other half of the interval carries no new information.
p = 1/2 (the srw point) and p = 1/3 (the headline) have their own recipes.
The budget here is deliberately smaller: the sieve asks where gamma_hat(p)
LEAVES 1/2, which a coarser error bar can answer, and the point that moves
is then re-run at the headline budget.
1/2, which a coarser error bar answers, and the top two rungs are 85% of
the cost. The point that moves is then re-run on the full ladder at the
headline budget.
LADDER 8..1024, NOT 32..4096 -- measured, 2026-09-15. A first pilot on
32..4096 reported 'a pure power law still fits (chi2/dof = 0.77, p = 0.60):
no correction visible yet for omega1 to be fitted to', and returned
omega1 = 0.033 +/- 0.012 against srw's exact 1. That is the pilot being
right: with a1 = -1/4 the correction to log E Y is a1/k = -0.8% at k = 32 and
-0.006% at k = 4096, while the per-scale noise at that budget was 1.6%. The
correction was below the noise at EVERY rung, so there was nothing to fit.
Starting at k = 8 puts the correction at -3.1% on the bottom rung, above the
noise, which is where experiments/01_srw measured omega1 = 1 in the first
place (its own pilot ladder is 8..256). The ladder is also 8x cheaper per
sample-column, so the same wall clock buys ~10x the samples. Powers of two
throughout: a grid that mixes parities fits the |X_k| staircase as curvature
and returns nonsense (tools/correction.py's CAUTION).
Extended down to k = 4 on the pilot's own advice (2026-09-15): on 8..1024 it
refused, reporting 'a pure power law still fits (chi2/dof = 2.67, p = 0.014):
no correction visible' with the departure at the bottom rung 0.0116 against
noise 0.0064, and said so in its own words -- 'more samples buy precision as
sqrt(n); a smaller rung buys it as a power of the scale'. At k = 4 the
one-correction truncation of eq. (232) still describes srw to 0.2% (exact
E|S_4| = 1.5 against a0*2*exp(a1/4) = 1.4967), so the rung is inside the
regime the model is allowed to be fitted on.
